items.headline: OHA Measles 31 Days Stale — School Window ~6 Days (~4 Operative); Gas OR $5.353 Record / WA $5.788 / National $4.564 Record (5th Consecutive Day); Portland $172M Shortfall; Memorial Day Compresses All Windows
items.summary: Three PNW threads. First: OHA measles reaches 31 days of publication staleness on Saturday May 23. Oregon Health Authority last published 20 confirmed cases on April 22 with no update since, despite the May 12 first Oregon hospitalization (patient discharged, recovering), ongoing Washington State outbreak (40+ cases, 8 counties, Kittitas County active), and national CDC count of 1,893 as of May 14. State epidemiologist Dr. Dean Sidelinger has characterized the 20 reported cases as 'just the tip of the iceberg.' The school vaccination window is approximately 6 calendar days; Memorial Day weekend removes two school-coordination days — leaving approximately 4 operative school days before logistical non-viability. Once the school year ends, the intervention landscape shifts permanently to outpatient and community health settings which cannot replicate the organizational speed or coverage scale of school-based campaigns. Any new county outbreak declaration, new Oregon hospitalization, or documented school-exposure event in the next 6 days constitutes a critical escalation with the window closing. Second: Oregon gasoline holds at $5.353 per gallon (record 2026 high), Washington at $5.788, national average at $4.564 (record 2026 high, rising for the fifth consecutive day). Memorial Day weekend driving demand is occurring at record fuel cost levels — accelerating household budget stress across PNW communities. Brent crude at approximately $106 and WTI at approximately $101 sustain the Hormuz-driven floor. No near-term pump relief: Trump's patience signal is not a pump-relief scenario; even a confirmed deal framework requires weeks of Hormuz transit normalization before retail prices respond. Third: Portland's $172 million city budget shortfall compounds under record energy costs ($5.353/gallon), 30-year Treasury above 5% raising municipal borrowing costs, and state revenue compression from the supply-shock economic slowdown. Memorial Day weekend provides no relief or policy response window.

analyst_summary: Saturday May 23, 2026 morning — Hormuz Day 85, Naval Blockade Day 42, Project Freedom Pause Day 18, WPA Day 24 Past Statutory Deadline / 6 Days to 90-Day Hard Deadline May 29, Warsh Day 9. Vibe 3. Memorial Day weekend Saturday: federal legislative channels closed through Monday May 26. The primary overnight development is the 5th round of US-Iran nuclear talks in Muscat, producing Iran's characterization from FM Araghchi that negotiations are 'complicated' and 'too complicated to resolve in two or three meetings.' The deal track remains structurally alive — both sides have affirmed continued discussion, Pakistan's Army Chief is now in Tehran for the highest-level direct military mediation engagement of the current cycle, and Oman continues as the primary diplomatic conduit — but the 'complicated' framing explicitly confirms that the structural gaps have not been resolved. Witkoff's dismantlement demand (Natanz, Fordow, Isfahan) remains categorically distinct from the 12-15-year moratorium that is the actual negotiating range; no US bilateral statement has engaged with that range directly. The congressional zero-enrichment constraint is not satisfied by a moratorium of any duration. No resumption order was issued; Trump's patience signal from May 21 holds. The WPA 90-day hard deadline is six days away. Congress does not return until May 26 — three calendar days before the deadline — and the next House war powers vote is explicitly scheduled for early June, after the deadline. At Day 90 on May 29, the war operates definitionally outside any credible statutory basis. Warsh enters his second weekend without a single public statement. The 10-year settled near 4.57% Friday; the 30-year settled near 5.07% after hitting 5.19% (2007 high) intraweek; markets price a 40% December hike probability. Gas hits record 2026 highs nationally ($4.564) and for Oregon ($5.353) and Washington ($5.788) as Memorial Day weekend driving demand occurs at peak cost. The May 12 CISA advisory (DIB/Israeli-linked target expansion) extended the known cyber threat surface; Memorial Day weekend reduces federal monitoring staffing within a fully-open IRGC cyber window. Oregon fire season is Day 16 with 9 days to east Cascades above-normal onset; 82% statewide drought with Southern Cascades at extreme; BLM Day 10 full restrictions; delegation letter 16 days unanswered; federal channels closed through the weekend. School vaccination window narrows to approximately 6 calendar days (~4 operative). Every structural negative is one day more advanced than yesterday. Vibe 3.

Warsh Day 10+: second weekend extends the communication vacuum; 40% December hike probability requires Warsh communication to price correctly; any scheduled speech, regional Fed president commentary, or Fed calendar update is the highest-priority domestic economic signal; June FOMC 25 days out

Gas prices — OR $5.353, WA $5.788, national $4.564 record 2026 highs; fifth consecutive daily increase entering Memorial Day weekend; watch AAA Oregon/Idaho and GasBuddy for sixth consecutive day signal; no near-term pump relief absent deal closure plus weeks of Hormuz transit normalization
